_label: Fun facts, all from cited Wikipedia articles (accessed 2026-10-10).

timeline: Founded as one of the American League's eight charter franchises (first known as the Boston Americans).
Beat the Pittsburgh Pirates in the first World Series.
Fenway Park opens; Red Sox win the World Series.
101 wins; beat the Phillies 4 games to 1 in the World Series.
Beat the Brooklyn Robins in the World Series.
Fifth title by 1918 - then the sale of Babe Ruth to the Yankees and the 'Curse of the Bambino' drought.
Reached the World Series with Ted Williams; lost to St. Louis (Enos Slaughter's 'mad dash').
The 'Impossible Dream' season.
AL pennant; Carlton Fisk's World Series home run.
World Series Game 6 and Bill Buckner's error.
Sold out 820 straight home games (May 15, 2003 to April 10, 2013), a pro sports record.
86-year wait ends with the sixth World Series title; came back on the Yankees in the ALCS.
World Series champions.
World Series champions.
World Series champions - first team with four titles in the 21st century; nine total.
history.rivalry: Yankees rivalry 100+ years: ALCS meetings in 1999 and 2003 (NYY) and 2004 (BOS); 2018 ALDS (BOS in 4); 2021 Wild Card Game (BOS). 1978: blew a 14-game lead, lost the one-game playoff.

timeline: First home uniform: a red sock silhouette with 'BOSTON' in white block letters (used one season).
'BOSTON' and 'RED SOX' in blocky red letters.
Ornate 'RED SOX' script home lettering debuts - still in use today.
Current cap and uniform set introduced; road uniforms use blue block letters.
Pullover era; road lettering switched to red home typeface; 1974-78 home pullovers with striped belt.
Pullovers dropped; road returns to blue block letters.
Red home-style lettering returns on the road; player names added on road backs (never on home whites).
Red alternate home jersey introduced.
Green St. Patrick's jersey's regular-season debut (Apr 20) honoring Red Auerbach.
Blue road alternate with red 'BOSTON' introduced; road lettering switched to blue; hanging-sox sleeve patch.
'BOSTON' + 'B STRONG' home jersey on Apr 20 after the Marathon bombing - now worn every Patriots' Day.
Road lettering back to red in the home font.
First Nike City Connect (Apr 6): yellow and light blue Marathon-inspired, '617' bib patch.
Blue alternates retired; yellow City Connect joins the core set; red alternates worn on the road for the first time (Mar 29 at Texas).
Second City Connect (May 16) inspired by the Green Monster: scoreboard font, '1912' in the collar, ball/strike dot colors.

facts: Opened
April 20, 1912 - Boston beat the New York Highlanders 7-6 in 11 innings.
Status
Oldest active ballpark in MLB; substantially rebuilt in 1934; on the National Register of Historic Places since March 7, 2012.
Green Monster
37 ft 2 in high left-field wall, 310 ft down the left-field line. The wall rose on the site of the leveled 'Duffy's Cliff'.
Pesky's Pole
Right-field foul pole, 302 ft. Named for Johnny Pesky (credit for the name goes to Mel Parnell), who hit some of his six Fenway homers near it.
The Triangle
Center-field corner 420 ft from home; true center (unmarked) is 390 ft.
Lone Red Seat
Section 42, Row 37, Seat 21 - Ted Williams' 502-ft homer on June 9, 1946.
Scoreboard
Hand-operated scoreboard in the Monster; NL scores removed in 1976 and restored in 2003.
Size
Fifth-smallest MLB park by seating capacity; one of nine that can't hold 40,000.
World Series
Hosted 11 World Series: Red Sox won six there, the Boston Braves one.
Other events
Football (Redskins, Yanks, Patriots), concerts, soccer, and the NHL Winter Classic in 2010 and 2023.
Address
Jersey Street (renamed Yawkey Way 1977-2018, then reverted).
Spring home
JetBlue Park at Fenway South, Fort Myers (since 2012) - identical dimensions and its own 37-ft Monster.
